Tolerance Intervals for Count Regression Models

Source: R/intervals.R
tolerance_interval.Rd

Content tolerance intervals for the observed count of a countreg() model: integer intervals intended to contain at least a fraction content of the count distribution at given covariate values, with confidence confidence over repeated samples.

Usage

tolerance_interval(
  object,
  newdata = NULL,
  content = 0.95,
  confidence = 0.95,
  side = c("two-sided", "upper", "lower"),
  scope = c("pointwise", "simultaneous"),
  method = c("auto", "joint", "envelope", "exact"),
  uncertainty = c("normal", "bootstrap"),
  npoints = 400,
  bootstraps = 200,
  seed = NULL,
  max_count = 1e+05
)

Arguments

object

a model fitted with countreg().

newdata

a data frame of covariate profiles (scenarios). Defaults to the training rows.

content

the required fraction \(p\) of the count distribution (e.g. 0.95).

confidence

the confidence level \(\gamma\) (e.g. 0.95).

side

"two-sided" (default), "upper" (interval [0, U]) or "lower" (interval [L, Inf)).

scope

"pointwise" (default): each row's interval has the stated confidence on its own; "simultaneous": the confidence holds jointly for all covariate profiles (based on a confidence set for all parameters, so wider).

method

"auto" (default): "exact" when it applies, otherwise "joint". "joint": the narrowest integer interval whose content is at least content for every parameter value in the confidence set. "envelope": equal-tail quantiles taken at the worst-case parameter values of each tail (simpler, more conservative). "exact": the common-rate Poisson construction, available for intercept-only Poisson models without auxiliary components.

uncertainty

how the confidence set is formed: "normal" (default), the asymptotic normal (Wald) confidence ellipsoid of the estimates, or "bootstrap", a parametric-bootstrap confidence region. "normal" switches to the bootstrap, with a message, when the covariance matrix is not positive definite.

npoints

number of points of the confidence set at which the distribution is evaluated (normal method). They are deterministic (based on Halton sequences), so results are reproducible.

bootstraps

number of parametric-bootstrap refits.

seed

random seed for the parametric bootstrap (the caller's random-number stream is not changed). NULL uses the current stream.

max_count

largest count used when resolving the upper tail.

Value

A data frame with one row per row of newdata: fit (the expected count), lower and upper (integer limits; upper is Inf for side = "lower"), min_content (the smallest content of the interval over the evaluated points of the confidence set) and status ("ok", or the reason a limit is unavailable). The settings are stored in the attribute "tolerance".

Details

What the interval means. For covariates \(x\), an integer interval \([L, U]\) computed from the estimation sample \(D\) is a content tolerance interval if $$\Pr_D\{F_\theta(U \mid x) - F_\theta(L - 1 \mid x) \ge p\} \ge \gamma,$$ where \(F_\theta\) is the distribution function of the observed count under the true parameters, \(p\) the content and \(\gamma\) the confidence. This differs from a prediction interval (which covers one future count on average; see predict.flexCountReg()) and from a confidence interval for the mean. The statement is conditional on the model being correct.

Construction. The distribution of the count at \(x\) depends on the parameters only through the linear predictors of the model components at \(x\) (mean, distribution-parameter formulas, reporting and zero models). A confidence set for those linear predictors is formed (Wald: an ellipsoid with \(\chi^2\) cutoff, with as many degrees of freedom as linear predictors for pointwise intervals, or as parameters for simultaneous intervals; bootstrap: the bootstrap draws closest to the estimate in Mahalanobis distance, a fraction \(\gamma\) of them). The distribution is evaluated at npoints points of the set (its boundary, interior and center; deterministic Halton-based points) and the interval is chosen so that its content is at least \(p\) at every evaluated point. When the true parameter lies in the confidence set the interval has the required content, so the confidence is approximately at least \(\gamma\); it is approximate because the confidence set is asymptotic (or bootstrap-based) and the extrema are found on a finite set of points. Discrete counts generally give more than the requested content; endpoints are never interpolated.

Exact Poisson method. For an intercept-only Poisson model (a common rate \(\lambda\), with exposures from an offset), an exact confidence interval for \(\lambda\) from stats::poisson.test() is mapped to Poisson quantiles at the scenario's exposure, giving an interval with at least the stated content and confidence (conservative because of discreteness).

In a Monte Carlo study of Poisson and NB2 regressions (n = 50 and 200, 1000 samples each; content 0.90, confidence 0.95), the joint method achieved confidence 0.99 to 1.00 and plug-in quantile intervals (which ignore estimation uncertainty) as little as 0.54. The interval targets the observed (reported) count, including zero-inflated, hurdle and underreporting components. Random-parameter and panel models are not yet supported.

References

Krishnamoorthy, K. and Mathew, T. (2009). Statistical Tolerance Regions: Theory, Applications, and Computation. Wiley.

Young, D. S. (2010). tolerance: An R package for estimating tolerance intervals. Journal of Statistical Software, 36(5), 1-39.

See also

predict.flexCountReg() for confidence and prediction intervals.

Examples

data("washington_roads")
fit <- countreg(Total_crashes ~ lnaadt + lnlength, data = washington_roads,
                family = "NB2", method = "BFGS")
scen <- data.frame(lnaadt = log(c(2000, 10000)), lnlength = log(1))
tolerance_interval(fit, scen, content = 0.90, confidence = 0.95)
#> Tolerance intervals: content 0.9, confidence 0.95, two-sided, pointwise
#> Method: joint (normal)
#>         fit lower upper min_content status
#> 1 0.4817664     0     2   0.9605277     ok
#> 2 2.9030182     0     8   0.9208960     ok

# Exact common-rate Poisson method
set.seed(1)
d <- data.frame(y = rpois(30, 2))
p0 <- countreg(y ~ 1, data = d, family = "POISSON", method = "BFGS")
tolerance_interval(p0, data.frame(x = 1), content = 0.95)
#> Tolerance intervals: content 0.95, confidence 0.95, two-sided, pointwise
#> Method: exact (exact)
#>   fit lower upper min_content status
#> 1   2     0     6   0.9836322     ok
